messages:
Rachel: FYI we're seeing recurring 429s on Tempo's dedicated cluster since ~17:01 UTC. Tokens/s SLO is failing — admission layer returning rejects; x-rw-burst-credits reported 0 for several accounts.

Darin: @Rachel can you paste a trace id or a quick repro?

Rachel: trace=tr-9f3a2b; quick repro curl (one request): `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-7b\",\"input\":\"hello\"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` -> HTTP/1.1 429
Headers: `x-rw-admit: reject`, `x-rw-burst-credits: 0`, `x-rw-node: gpx-17`

Meenal: I see GPU mem pressure and KV cache misses on gpx-17 around the same time. p95 token latency climbed to ~1.8s. Possible noisy neighbor hitting memory and causing slow KV lookups.

infra-bot: [ALERT] pool=tempo-prod headroom=0. autoscaler: no recent scale-up events.

Darin: Can we get autoscaler logs? @srebot

srebot: autoscale log snippet: `2026-03-17T16:58:00Z avg_gpu_util=78% threshold=80% min_replicas=4 -> no scale`; burst credits depleted due to many short bursts from several API keys. No policy triggered because avg util < threshold.

Ryan: From the admission perspective, token bucket refill was tuned for steady-state. These customers have many short high-QPS sessions so they exhaust burst credits much faster than refill rate. Suggest raising account-level refill or increasing headroom.

Julia: Also noticed several 502s from auth proxy at 17:01:20-17:02:05 — some clients retried aggressively, amplifying bursts. Correlate with billing? @billing (cc: @support)

Rachel: Billing shows no unexpected invoice spikes, but logs show repeated auth 502s for a handful of keys, which matches the start of the SLO violations.

Darin: Immediate mitigation: paused low-priority background tasks in pool, manually scaled pool +2 replicas, and temporarily allowed fallback to hosted endpoint for canary routes. Did that change reject rate?

Rachel: After manual scale and pausing jobs p95 dropped back to ~350ms and we started seeing `x-rw-burst-credits: 1200` in responses. Reqs that were 429 are now succeeding.

Meenal: Repro steps for on-call to validate locally: 
1) Run parallel load: `seq 1 200 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I% curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code} %{time_total}\\n\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-7b\"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate`
2) Watch metrics: `kubectl top pods -n tempo-prod` and `rwctl metrics --pool tempo-prod --metric=burst_credits --tail 60`
3) Check logs: `kubectl logs -l app=admission --since=5m` and `rwctl traces --trace-id tr-9f3a2b`

Darin: Long-term remediation suggestions:
- Make token-bucket refill per-account configurable (and higher default for bursty customers)
- Add adaptive autoscaler rule to consider short-timescale bursts (e.g., spike detection)
- Implement noisy-neighbor detection on GPU memory pressure and evict or migrate offending workloads
- Harden auth proxy retry behavior to reduce amplification

Ryan: I'll open a PR for per-account refill config + metrics dimensions. Assigning probe of KV cache hotspots and eviction logic to @Meenal.

Julia: Filed support incident INC-7241; notification sent to customer with mitigation steps and ETA for postmortem.

Rachel: Saved traces and logs to https://logs.redwood.example/tempo/2034567890; adding timeline and exporting relevant kube metrics to the ticket.

infra-bot: action:manual_scale +2 -> completed by darin@17:03 UTC

srebot: incident status -> resolved (monitoring) ; follow-up window 30m

Rachel: Thanks team — marking this for a postmortem and follow-up with product for prewarm / min_replicas recommendations.
